xfixium wrote

Aye, excellent question. I think I may have done the palette design at least 4 times.


Thanks for sharing the complete set that you have generated, this clearly shows how much work you put into maximizing visibility. I think everything works well indeed, except maybe for a couple "orange" enemies on the dungeon BG. I suppose that you may plan different palettes for the BG ? Of course, they will not be strictly palette swaps. But this could help the few cases as you will know which enemy appears on which BG color. The dams also have color themes, this would work well.

Funny that you mention the color purple by the way, because when making the Sword of Stone, I ended up in a similar situation and the game did not have any purple at all. This frustrated me to no end.

A final thing I want to say in case some people don't realize this, is that targetting the same ROM size as on MegaDrive might prove challenging because you cannot use palette swaps for the various palettes of a single enemy : they are actually redrawn using different indexes of the palette. If I were you I wouldn't bother at all with trying to reach such a ROM a size for now and simply keep it below 1 MB.

entry.content:
Author: segarule
Posted: Tue Nov 10, 2026 9:01 am (GMT 0)

xfixium wrote
A demo is out, but not too much going on, it's basically a walking demo. You can visit a bunch of areas on Mota. Paseo, Oputa, Arima, Shure, Nido, and the Bio Systems lab. All the bridges are open, so you can explore most of Mota, except the areas that require the Jet Scooter. Random encounters happen. Pressing button 1 escapes the battle, button 2 cycles through 3 different test battle backgrounds. Pressing button 1 opens the menu when on the field. The only other menu available is the SYS menu. You can select the walking speed you desire from there. No data driven dialog text yet. The continue menu is just a mock up with no code behind it yet.

I had this close to a demo about roughly a year ago. But as luck would have it, my laptop died, and my motivation went out the window with it. But the last few weeks or so, I looked at the remaining items of my demo ready todo list, and got it done.

Some notes about it's current state. Most of the graphics conversion is done for the Mota towns. There are things I still want to adjust and redo however. The overworld will get a total re-vamp at some point. The battle backgrounds are placeholders. Except the VR one, which I consider done. The grass bg one is a PS1 bg, with some edits. The dungeon bg is a PSIV bg edited. So those will eventually be original graphics. Some of the enemies still need some TLC. I condensed the menus to save on RAM and screen real estate. Most main character sprites are done, or just need a little tweaking. Just missing Kain and Hugh. Probably some other notes I'm missing XD. I think that's it, for now.

Thanks for viewing.

Download Link:
https://pyxosoft.com/projects/sms_ps2/downloads/sms_phantasy_star_ii.sms

Demo vid:
https://pyxosoft.com/projects/sms_ps2/videos/psii_0010.mp4

Amazing! Im curious in see the battle system working! Congratulations

entry.title: Development :: RE: SMS Phantasy Star II
entry.dc:creator: xfixium
entry.dc:subject: Development
entry.content:
Author: xfixium
Posted: Tue Nov 10, 2026 6:56 am (GMT 0)

cireza wrote
Hello xfixium,

The demo has a great presentation, the visuals have a lot of contrast and volume.

I was wondering if you had planned, and how, the rest of the battle content. Meaning backgrounds and enemies. Specifically about color choices.

I can see that you have locked in 13 colors that have to be common between characters and enemies, which means all backgrounds will have to be implemented with these 13 colors. For merging purposes if I understand.

This leaves 3 possible variable slots : are you planning to change them dynamically to be able to add an original color in the background and/or ennemies ? Or will these be set in stone ?

Simply wondering this because of some color gradients used for some enemies or potential backgrounds, and how you are going to work around these. Making ReSeCom, I found out that colors between my monsters/characters and the background happened to clash pretty often, and as neither were underlined with black (for a more realistic approach) I often had to make specific palette swaps to be sure of having the best visibility. And this happened despite the fact that I was actually reserving dedicated colors for background (7) and others for the enemies (9).


Aye, excellent question. I think I may have done the palette design at least 4 times. Eventually I ended up with just a static 16 BG palette. Which does the job, but it removes the purples from certain enemies. Instead swapping out to reds for most. I prioritized keeping as much of the graphic detail as possible. I have touched up various enemies, adding dithering where needed. As some enemies use quite a lot of gradients.

There was some concern when BG and enemy graphics use the same palette. For my own sanity, I made a script that runs the game through all the enemy formations and BGs, and for the most part, it looks fine. It also is a bit early for me, because those BGs will be replaced at some point, and there is still future challenges like the colored dams. Maybe my saving grace is that I have the option to use black, and the few issues I have, can be corrected with some creative outlining.

In my notes I have marked down:
mota BG:
burnwolf, rabitta, bleeds into BG

dungeon BG:
sonomech, wirehead, firgamma, rabbit, can get lost in BG

Image output samples (If you're interested):
https://pyxosoft.com/projects/sms_ps2/images/enemy_formations.zip

entry.title: Development :: RE: [AI] New programming language MasterBASIC
entry.dc:creator: wolf83
entry.dc:subject: Development
entry.content:
Author: wolf83
Subject: An opition about AI usage
Posted: Mon Nov 09, 2026 9:07 pm (GMT 0)

I understand that manual programming and using certain programming languages has its own aesthetics and nostalgia and the nostalgia is why we are here for. Also, code that we understand has a benefit. However, AI opens totally new possibilities in this community and only with AI many ideas and projects can be realistically finished. There are many projects and postings which people have started and then gave up on them due to lack of time, effort, expertise, and other limited resources. People just do not have sufficient time and persistence to realize or finish projects, or to go beyond basic prototypes, but with AI they could. Choosing the programming language, programming style, or hand-made code, quality of contributions are orthogonal topics to AI. For example, why can a person A not write hand-made code, if person B uses AI. Person A can make a good or bad contribution with hand-made code, person B can make a good or bad contribution with AI. These things are independent.

My personal recommendation is to support AI usage in this forum (not for competitions) and to think how to prepare good instructions for AI so it understands how to work with the hardware and instructions effectively and enable projects. This would enable also non-experts to realize their long time wishes, that no person will otherwise implement. I am a programmer, but I do not have the time to study the hardware and all the programming that would be necessary for project that I would like to implement or mod in existing games. I would be happy to see am extensive knowledge base (agent skill) for an AI agent so it could realize the things that I would like to implement for my Game Gear. Also I have been waiting here for some projects to be finished and it never happened in the end, so the argument is real.

This is just my opinion and recommendation.
